title: Most Cocktails Fail Here (And It’s Not the Alcohol)
subtitle: If your drink tastes off, this is probably why.
summary:
Most people assume a bad cocktail comes down to the alcohol. It doesn’t. It’s almost always balance. Too sweet, too sharp, too flat — something is just slightly off, and it throws the whole drink.

Once you understand how ratios actually work, everything gets easier. You stop guessing, and your drinks start tasting intentional.

sections.title: It’s Not About the Recipe, It’s About the Ratio
sections.body:
Recipes are helpful, but they’re not the whole story. The real structure of a cocktail comes from how the ingredients relate to each other.

Once you understand the ratio behind a drink, you can adjust it, fix it, or even build your own without starting from scratch.

sections.title: The Basic Balance: Strong, Sweet, Sour
sections.body:
Most cocktails follow a simple structure: spirit for strength, sugar for sweetness, and citrus for brightness.

If one of those is too heavy or too light, the drink feels off. The goal isn’t perfection — it’s balance that feels natural when you take a sip.

sections.title: Why Drinks Taste ‘Off’
sections.body:
If a drink is too sharp, it usually needs more sweetness or dilution. If it’s too sweet, it probably needs more acid or a stronger base.

Most issues aren’t dramatic — they’re small imbalances that add up.

sections.title: Start With a Simple Ratio
sections.body:
A good place to start is 2 parts spirit, 3/4 part citrus, and 1/2 part sweet. From there, you adjust based on taste and the ingredients you’re using.

This works for a lot of drinks, especially sours, and it gives you a solid starting point instead of guessing.

sections.title: Taste and Adjust — Every Time
sections.body:
Even when you know the ratio, ingredients change. Lemons vary, spirits differ, and small shifts matter.

Taste your drink, adjust slightly, and pay attention. That’s how you get better quickly.
